{{Top|leg|notoc=1}}
'''Mandalorian poetry''' was poetry composed by members of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] culture, often in their native [[Language/Legends|language]], ''[[Mando'a/Legends|Mando'a]]''.

Poetic or sung ''Mando'a'' was considerably more free-form than the language was more commonly spoken, and while the meaning of these works were easily understood by native speakers as most songs and poems were embedded in the broader culture, they could become difficult for non-Mandalorians to properly translate.<ref name="TMPaC">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Mandalorian poetry was first discussed in ''[[The Mandalorians: People and Culture]]'', written by [[Karen Traviss]] and published in [[2006]] as part of the [[Star Wars Insider 86|eighty-sixth issue]] of ''[[Star Wars Insider]]''.<ref name="TMPaC" />

[[Jeffrey Brown]]'s [[Canon|non-canonical]] childrens' novel [[Jedi Academy (novel)|''Jedi Academy'']] by [[Jeffrey Brown]] states that the study of Mandalorian poetry was a requirement for [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]] at the [[Jedi academy]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="academy">[[Jedi Academy (novel)|''Jedi Academy'']]</ref>
